clue.text: Like monarch travelling without a case?

blocks.note: first meaning: away from the royal court, as a king on a journey would be
second meaning: settled privately, with no lawsuit heard by a judge

explanation.surface: A king on tour with no luggage to carry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' looks like a suitcase for the travelling monarch; it is a legal case.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes both absence from a royal household and a dispute settled privately before any trial.

clue.text: Discomfort of crowned head in retirement

definitions.text: Discomfort of crowned head in retirement

blocks.clueFragment: Discomfort of crowned head in retirement
blocks.note: surface reading: a king who has stepped down from the throne feels ill at ease
setter's reading: retirement is going to bed, recalling Shakespeare's line about the head that wears a crown lying uneasily

explanation.surface: An abdicated king feels uncomfortable in his retired life.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry IV, Part 2 has 'Uneasy lies the head that wears a crown'; retiring here means lying down for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names a state of anxious discomfort, the feeling the sleepless crowned king is said to suffer.

clue.text: Hero's heartfelt cry in the shrubbery?

definitions.note: the answer is one shrub, not a planting of them

blocks.note: the exclamation O, a cry from the heart
in Greek myth Hero's lover swam the Hellespont nightly to reach her

explanation.surface: A heroine sighs a passionate cry while hiding among the bushes.
explanation.walkthrough: Hero is the priestess of the myth, not any brave person; her heartfelt cry would be 'O Leander!'
explanation.definitionFit: The oleander is an evergreen flowering shrub, so it belongs in any shrubbery.

clue.text: Make sword safer for man held in field

blocks.note: first meaning: put something over the sharp tip of a blade
second meaning: a cricket fielding position, and the player stationed there

explanation.surface: Blunting a weapon to protect a soldier kept prisoner in the field.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, cover point is a fielding position on the off side, square of the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricket term names a fielding position and the player placed there; read literally it means sheathing a blade's tip.

clue.text: Cockney's description of Dobermann is faulty

indicators.note: a Londoner of the East End drops initial aitches, so this tells us to say the words in that accent

blocks.note: a Dobermann is a German breed of dog, a Hun's hound; said with the aitches dropped

explanation.surface: A Londoner describes a Dobermann as an unreliable dog.
explanation.walkthrough: Hun is an old slang term for a German; a Cockney drops the h from both Hun's and hound.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsound and faulty are synonyms: flawed, not in good working condition or reasoning.

clue.text: Times leader to back US President

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of the newspaper's name
aft means at the back, as of a ship

explanation.surface: The newspaper's editorial supports an American president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times leader' reads as the paper's editorial, but it is just its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: William Howard Taft was the 27th president of the United States, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Base line situated in middle of oriental island

indicators.note: something situated in the middle of another word sits inside it, with letters on both sides

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A survey line is drawn across the centre of an eastern island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base line' reads as one phrase; split it and put the second word inside the first, after BA.
explanation.definitionFit: Balinese describes people, things or language from Bali, an island in Indonesia.

clue.text: Controller reported back In former position

blocks.note: a rein is the strap that controls a horse
to report something is to state it

explanation.surface: A manager has reported back to the board from his old job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reported back' looks like one phrase; 'back' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone reinstated has been restored to an earlier job or rank after removal.

clue.text: Burning a mark on horse

blocks.note: taken as written
a blaze is a white stripe down a horse's face

explanation.surface: Branding a horse with a hot iron.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ablaze is on fire, flames rising from it, the same as burning.

clue.text: Misleads rich man about EEC members

indicators.note: taking the members of a group singly lets them stand in any order
about means round the outside, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: Dives is the rich man in Jesus's parable of Lazarus
the European Economic Community, taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: A wealthy man lies about the countries of the Common Market.
explanation.walkthrough: The three letters go in after the D of the rich man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To deceive someone is to mislead them, making them believe something untrue.

clue.text: Vacation ordered for emperor-to-be

indicators.note: ordered means arranged afresh, so the letters are put into a new sequence

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A holiday is prescribed for the heir to the throne.
explanation.definitionFit: Octavian was the name of Rome's first emperor before he took the title Augustus, so he was the future ruler.

clue.text: Start preparing Wimbledon court for this player

blocks.note: first meaning: sow grass on a lawn tennis court
second meaning: a ranked tennis entrant kept apart in the draw

explanation.surface: Groundsmen get a Wimbledon court ready for a particular player.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon is the London grass-court tennis championship, where top players are ranked in the draw.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to sow, the first step for a grass lawn; the noun is a ranked tennis competitor.

clue.text: Tapestries arranged in barely finished display

indicators.note: arranged means set out in a fresh order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Wall hangings hung for a show that was only just completed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barely finished' reads as 'only just completed'; here it means ending up bare.
explanation.definitionFit: A performance of undressing ends with the performer nearly naked, so the show finishes bare.

clue.text: Second part of Dostoevsky's book fitting the first?

definitions.text: Second part of Dostoevsky's book fitting the first?

blocks.note: surface reading: the later volume of a Russian novel
setter's reading: the second word of the title Crime and ..., which should fit the first word, as the proverb says

explanation.surface: A reader asks whether a novel's sequel lives up to its opening volume.
explanation.walkthrough: The novel is Crime and Punishment; the saying is 'let the punishment fit the crime'.
explanation.definitionFit: The penalty imposed for wrongdoing is the second word of the title and is supposed to match the crime.

clue.text: Desire etc, the reverse of smart in USA

definitions.text: the reverse of smart in USA

blocks.note: first meaning: Desire is the tram in Tennessee Williams's play A Streetcar Named Desire, one example of many

blocks.clueFragment: the reverse of smart in USA
blocks.note: second meaning: smart read backwards is trams, and Americans call trams by another name

explanation.surface: Longing and the like are the opposite of being clever in America.
explanation.walkthrough: Desire looks like a feeling; it is the named vehicle of the play.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans use this word for city trams running on rails, and the play's title names one such vehicle.

clue.text: A burden to forgo

blocks.note: first meaning: the chorus repeated after each verse of a song
second meaning: hold back from doing something

explanation.surface: Giving something up feels like a heavy load.
explanation.walkthrough: Burden is an old word for a song's repeated chorus, not a load.
explanation.definitionFit: A song's recurring chorus is called both names; as a verb the word means abstain or hold back.

clue.text: Man, perhaps, has just put on jersey

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece put on another sits above it, so it comes first

blocks.note: fair and just both mean even-handed
the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea, is an example of an island

explanation.surface: A man has just pulled on a sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: Man is the island, and Jersey looks like another island; here it is a sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: A Fair Isle is a knitted sweater with bands of coloured pattern, named after the Shetland island.

clue.text: Display outstanding quality in scheme

blocks.note: first meaning: stick out, the quality of something standing out from a surface
second meaning: a planned undertaking

explanation.surface: Show exceptional merit in a planned venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' means excellent on the surface but literally standing out.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means jut out; as a noun it is a planned piece of work or enterprise.

clue.text: European, vessel also turned up before five

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning a word up makes it read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a jug is a vessel for liquid
taken as written
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A European jug was also discovered ahead of five others.
explanation.walkthrough: The older spelling of Yugoslav, with a J, is the one this grid needs.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jugoslav came from Yugoslavia, a former Balkan country, so is one example of a European.

clue.text: Way Father upset Holy See

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset means turned upside down, so the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a mode is a way of doing something
pop is an informal word for a father

explanation.surface: The way a priest disturbed the Vatican.
explanation.walkthrough: Father looks like a priest, which fits the Vatican picture, but it is a dad.
explanation.definitionFit: The Holy See is the jurisdiction and office of the pope, which is what the word for his office denotes.

clue.text: Refuge for those, after Reformation, in dreadful peril

indicators.note: a re-formation is a forming again, so the letters are formed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hiding place for Catholics who were endangered after the Protestant Reformation.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital R makes it look like the historical Reformation, which is also exactly when these hiding places were built.
explanation.definitionFit: Catholic priests in Elizabethan England hid from searchers in concealed chambers built into country houses.

clue.text: As financially sound as gold?

blocks.note: surface reading: solvent, a safe investment
setter's reading: the saying about a well-behaved child, 'as ... as gold'

explanation.surface: Is an investment as safe as bullion?
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb describes a child behaving well; the word also means creditworthy, as in a sound risk.
explanation.definitionFit: A creditworthy borrower or debt is called this, and the proverb compares a well-behaved child to gold.

clue.text: Player who calls a dob is such a batsman

blocks.note: first meaning: in bridge, the player who makes the first call of the auction
second meaning: in cricket, one of the pair who start the innings

explanation.surface: A card player who makes a call is a certain kind of cricketer.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan reads 'a dob', almost certainly a misprint or misreading of 'a bid'; the bridge player who calls the first bid of an auction has this name.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge the first bidder starts the auction; in cricket the first two batsmen start the innings.

clue.text: Final address for house

blocks.note: surface reading: the last postal location of a home
setter's reading: the audience in a theatre, spoken to at the end of a play

explanation.surface: The last postal address a home will have.
explanation.walkthrough: House means the theatre audience, and address means a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A closing speech delivered by an actor to the audience after a play has ended carries this name.

clue.text: Animal to attack, in a word

blocks.note: first meaning: a horned farm creature
second meaning: the two-word verb meaning attack, written as one

explanation.walkthrough: 'Go at' means to attack; run its two words together.
explanation.definitionFit: The goat is a horned, bearded farm creature, an example of the animal; the phrasal verb means set upon.

clue.text: Time limit for telephone fault

blocks.note: first meaning: the latest time by which work must be done
second meaning: a phone connection with no dialling tone

explanation.surface: A cutoff time set for reporting a broken phone.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a cutoff date for finishing work, and read as two words a phone link that has gone silent.

clue.text: Mouth-watering mainly vegetable dish four tucked into

definitions.note: read as a noun: the watering of the mouth

indicators.note: mainly means for the most part, so the end of the word is dropped
something tucked into another is placed inside it

blocks.note: a salad is a dish of raw vegetables
IV is the Roman numeral for four

explanation.surface: An appetising salad has four extra items mixed in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mouth-watering' looks like an adjective praising the dish; it is the definition, read as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Spit is the fluid the glands release when the mouth waters at the sight of food.

clue.text: Paper asserts they speed things up

blocks.note: The Times is a newspaper
to aver is to assert

explanation.surface: A newspaper claims that some things make work quicker.
explanation.definitionFit: Devices or shortcuts that cut the hours a task takes are what make work go faster.
